items.text: $u$ a section of $\mathcal A_{S'}$ = a homomorphism $\mathcal O_{S'}\to\mathcal A_{S'}$, dually a linear map $H_{S'}\to\mathcal O_{S'}$, $H=\mathcal A^\vee$ an algebra (the diagonal of $\mathcal A$ gives its product). The conditions $\varepsilon(u)=1$, $\pi(u)=u\otimes u$ say exactly that it is an algebra homomorphism:

$G=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal A$ commutative, finite, locally free: $D(G)=\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal A^\vee)$; the multiplication of $\mathcal A$ gives the diagonal of $\mathcal A^\vee$, hence the composition law of $D(G)$.
$G$ not commutative: $H$ is not commutative; $D(G)=\operatorname{Spec}H^{ab}$ (quotient by commutators), not locally free in general.

For $\mathcal A$ locally free of finite type, the axioms on multiplication and comultiplication are self-dual (the multiplication commutative; the comultiplication commutative as well for commutative $G$): $\mathcal A\mapsto\mathcal A^\vee$ is an involution on the category of commutative finite locally free monoids over $S$.
Over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z$, $\mu_n$ is not constant for $n>1$ (the fibres in characteristic dividing $n$ are not reduced).
\text{char }p:\quad D(\mu_p)=\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z\quad(\mu_p\ \text{infinitesimal},\ \mathbb Z/p\ \text{an ordinary finite group})
